It carries one generic group and roughly 60 named-bot groups. There is NO group naming ClaudeBot, Claude-Web, Claude-User, Claude-SearchBot or anthropic-ai anywhere in the file, and no Content-Signal line, so no Claude opt-out exists and there is no hard stop. The 'Bloquage Robots indesirables' block (adequat, ADmantX, BacklinkCrawler, Corporama, DotBot, ellisphere, EtaoSpider, Fetch, Grapeshot, houzzbot, infoseek, Jetbot, k2spider, leadbox, linkfluence, linko, Mail.Ru, Meltwater, MSIECrawler, NPBot, Nutch, opinion-tracker, proxem, Proximic, rogerbot, SeznamBot, SiteSnagger, spotter, SputnikBot, SurveyBot, Teleport, Updownerbot, verticalsearch, WebCopier, WebReaper, WebStripper, WebZIP, wget, winello, XoviBot, YisouSpider, Zealbot) and the price-scraper block (Net veille, Paarly, SpyCommerce, Pricing Assistant, Price Observatory, Workit, Keox, Pricejet, Prixan) each carry Disallow: / under THEIR OWN user-agent, none of which is us. Crawl-delay: 10 appears only under Baiduspider, YandexBot, archive.org_bot, MJ12bot, AhrefsBot, Soso and Sogou - not under '*' - so no crawl-delay is owed; probe.py's 2 s per-host gap was kept anyway and the run was in practice far slower than that. The '*' group disallows /basket, /checkout/*, /customer/*, /search?*, *Ns=*, *Nrpp=*, *sortByValue=*, *?*page=1&*, *isSearchResult=*, /*/reviews, /*/ratings/*, /*/price-*, /*/livraison-a-domicile/*, /*/en-magasin/*, /*/retrait-en-magasin/*, /product/productcomparison*, /stock-checker/*, *jsessionid*, *skuId*, *_DARGS*, *bvstate*, and a long list of double-facet patterns. NOTHING disallowed was requested: every URL fetched is a bare /.../cat_id_XXXX.cat category path with no query string at all - no Ns=, no Nrpp=, no sortByValue, no page=, no search, no basket/customer/checkout, no reviews/ratings/price/store-fulfilment path. Single host throughout (www.castorama.fr); the declared sitemap https://www.castorama.fr/fstrz/sm/sitemap-index.xml is on the same host, so no second robots.txt was owed. ACCESS: probe.fetch() with rotating curl_cffi fingerprints returned HTTP 200 on all 167 category requests - zero 403, zero 429, zero failures - but Castorama throttles hard: pages are 1.4-1.6 MB server-rendered React and response time degraded from ~4 s to 4-5 minutes per page over the run, which is why the crawl was checkpointed line-by-line to a JSONL file and resumed rather than held in memory. No reader prefix, no campaign parameter, no CORS proxy and no browser automation were used or needed. TREE: built top-down from Castorama's OWN artefacts and cross-checked two ways. (a) The category sitemap declared in robots.txt, https://www.castorama.fr/fstrz/sm/sitemap-cat.xml (4,841 s), of which 97 are hierarchical /salle-de-bains-et-wc/... category paths - that is the spine. (b) The mega-menu on /salle-de-bains-et-wc/cat_id_3322.cat and every hub page's own 'wcms-grid-category-tile' child strip, which is what recovers the branches the mega-menu TRUNCATES behind 'En voir plus' and the children that exist only as short-form URLs absent from the hierarchical sitemap slice - e.g. the four Porte de douche types (coulissante/pivotante/battante/pliante), the six Receveur de douche types, the four Colonne de douche types, the five Robinet de baignoire types, Vasque à poser/à encastrer/à suspendre, Lavabo suspendu/colonne/lave-mains, Plan simple/double/lave-mains vasque, Baignoire à porte, Baignoire douche, WC PMR, Pack WC suspendu, Ensemble lave-mains and Lot accessoires. 167 category pages were opened in total. PARENTAGE was NOT inferred from URL shape - it is read from each page's own JSON-LD BreadcrumbList, which is why nodes whose URL is a bare short form (e.g. /vasque-a-poser/) are still placed correctly under Salle de bains et WC > Lavabo, vasque et plan vasque. Two nodes are placed by breadcrumb rather than by URL: Serviette de bain (URL under accessoires, breadcrumb under Linge de bain) and Tablette et étagère de salle de bains (breadcrumb under Meuble de salle de bains, URL and children under Accessoires) - the latter is recorded ONCE, as a grouping row above its two children, per rule 28. Three breadcrumb levels have no URL of their own and are emitted as pure grouping rows: Baignoire, Lave-mains and Tablette et étagère. QTY: the listing page's OWN rendered total, read from the element Castorama prints above its grid - N produits. Nothing was estimated, no parent number was reused for a child and no siblings were summed. Castorama is a marketplace as well as a DIY chain (its sitemap index carries 15 separate 'newmkp' product sitemaps), which is why absolute counts are large; that is what the page shows and it is what is recorded. VERIFICATION: counts discriminate sharply and are not a site-wide constant - within the Baignoire branch alone: 2,124 / 1,441 / 1,188 / 663 / 174 / 8; within Douche: 6,155 / 4,310 / 2,030 / 953 / 170; and the smallest recorded leaves are 3 (Abattant WC clipsable, Vasque à suspendre), 5 (Pont de baignoire, Support et fixation miroir) and 6 (Porte de douche PMR, Fleur de douche, Armoire à pharmacie). Every recorded page's H1 was read and matches the node - e.g. H1 'Baignoire droite' on cat_id_766, H1 'Miroir lumineux' on cat_id_0001976 - and the products on the sample checked are on-category (Baignoire droite renders Horyn / GoodHome Teesta / Jacob Delafon Sofa straight tubs). Where a hub genuinely renders no grid the page prints no count element at all, which is exactly how the 13 grouping levels were identified rather than assumed. Every recorded link is the page's own rel=canonical string, verified per page, so the canonical-alias dedup blind spot is closed - the short-form URLs were dedup-checked in their canonical form, not in a nav-alias form.
